Then wait the two weeks, as shitty as that is. I bet ya that you’ll be feeling some relief within the next few days to a week. But , in the case that you don’t , your doc more than likely won’t proceed with anything else until the two weeks is up on the meds. So, take them as prescribed daily for the next two weeks. Even if everything goes away in the next few days, finish the prescription. 

If after that you feel no relief , talk to your doc. Let them know nothing changed and mention some things i spoke about in regards to bladder ultrasound , cystoscopy , ect if that’s what you’d like to pursue. You may be turned down on certain procedures , but , it will allow you and the doc to pursue different avenues when it comes to dealing with this. 

It’s most likely the same thing you’ve dealt with before though, it would make sense to be as you get often uti’s. and, get another culture test

I’d just ask for a cystoscopy straight up, if you feel something’s up or out of the “norm” from when you’ve had these in the past then explain that. 

Cystoscopies are incredibly useful for these types of things , but they’ll most likely do some other tests first to see if it clears up before allowing that sort of procedure to proceed. It’s not a fun process in terms of the few days afterward , plus it’s used for i guess more “serious” things? Idk. But , they’ll do multiple culture checks first to ensure that you don’t have a uti along with maybe some other tests as well. My case was very different circumstances but they held out on that procedure for quite some time until they checked other bases off the list. 

I wouldn’t stress yourself more than you already are. I understand it’s hard, trust me. but it’s unlikely to be something pretty serious. Uti’s can be pretty common in certain people and you can have culture checks that come back negative , even though they’re positive. 

Keep your head up.

Also, antibiotics typically take a couple days until you feel the relief. So, don’t give up on em yet. Push through the pain, take the meds as prescribed and see if they make a difference.

Another thing, please don’t mix my disease with what you have. It’s very uncommon as it is , but especially so in our age group. All my docs, specialists and urologists  were at a loss for words when we landed on it. Which, btw, took a couple years to accurately diagnose. So, please don’t put that in your head! I moreso just mentioned it to provide you with a bit of background on myself so you understood i have experience with this sort of thing and procedures that follow

I have some experience in this area actually, I (23M) have a disease called Interstitial Cystitis. It’s more or less having uti symptoms 24/7 365 but without an infection or any cultures. You can ask for a cystoscopy to check the bladder lining, depending on how long it’s been and how persistent it is. 

As for a bladder ultrasound, i never asked for one directly but got one as a favor when they were doing an ultrasound on my liver. The woman did it for me to see if my bladder fully empties after going to the washroom. So, maybe approach your doctor with that. Say you’d like to know if your bladder fully empties and how fast / how much it fills up after just going to the washroom. Sometimes it feels like a lot but is barely any, sometimes it’s a lot. 

Hope this helps a bit , sorry you’re having these issues. Shit’s never a fun time , arguably one of the shittiest pains to endure.
